text:
Tina Chen: quick heads-up — I ran a p50/p95 sweep for llm-v2-int8 across H100 vs A100 in us-east/us-west/eu-west. seeing a consistent p95 skew when requests route through edge-pop-usw. attaching quick numbers below, need brainpower on kernel selection vs routing policy.
Marco O.: share numbers pls and how you routed test traffic?
Tina Chen: was a synthetic QPS=120 steady stream, seq_len=1024 median prompt. routing: direct -> regional proxy -> edge-pop-usw forced path. recorded per-token lat_hist and total resp lat.
Jia Li: can you paste p50/p95 summary?
Tina Chen: H100 (us-east direct): p50 82ms p95 210ms | H100 (us-west via edge-usw): p50 95ms p95 380ms | A100 (us-east direct): p50 110ms p95 330ms | A100 (eu-west via edge-usw proxy->eu): p50 140ms p95 520ms
Rachel S.: whoa p95 jump for A100 eu-west. are KV cache warms identical?
Tina Chen: yes cold-warm states controlled: 80% warm, warmup threads prefill KV. verified similar token gen counts.
Marco O.: any kernel fallback or different fused-attn kernels selected when routed via edge? maybe different sequence chunking causing kernel path change.
Jia Li: dug into runtime logs — found this snippet when requests hit the edge proxy: 
```
[2026-01-08T14:02:33Z] model_dispatch: selected_kernel_set=huggingface_fused_v2
[2026-01-08T14:02:33Z] batcher: batch_size=12 latency_est=22ms policy=continuous
[2026-01-08T14:02:33Z] fallback: using_scalar_attention=false
```
But when routed direct, kernel set was huggingface_fused_v3 with kernel_epoch=7.
Rachel S.: so routing correlates with kernel selection. maybe runtime sees different sequence length distribution because proxy injects small batching jitter.
Marco O.: also check hop count and TLS termination location. edge-pop-usw decrypts and re-encrypts -> extra per-request CPU and context switch. add ~40–80ms tail per request under contention.
Tina Chen: I captured tcpdump RTTs: us-east direct -> median RTT 12ms; via edge-usw -> median RTT 48ms (plus jitter). aligns with added p95.
Jia Li: for quant path, int8 kernels on A100 show more sensitivity to batch shape. If routing alters per-batch shape (12->7), kernel chooses non-fused fallback that hits slower GEMM.
Rachel S.: proposal: change routing policy to prefer regional-proxy->local GPU for latency-sensitive models, or force kernel pinning at model-config to lock fused_v3 on A100/H100. Can we try a canary?
Tina Chen: +1. I can push config: {"model":"llm-v2-int8","kernel_hint":"fused_v3","routing_policy":"regional_prefer"} to a 5% canary in us-west and eu-west.
Marco O.: also validate warmup sequences to ensure batch shapes match production histogram. run load at QPS=200 for 10m to expose tail.
Jia Li: I'll instrument runtime to emit kernel choice metric (kernel_set) and batch_shape histogram per-pop. would help correlate quickly.
ops-bot: Deploy plan created: canary=5% / targets=[us-west-eu-west] / rollout=manual / ticket=OPS-4123
Rachel S.: quick checklist before canary: 1) kernel_hint param set 2) warmup corpus replayed 3) monitoring alarms for p95 > baseline+150ms 4) fallback auto-rollback on error spike
Tina Chen: starting canary prep now. I'll post results in this thread in ~30m. thanks all :thumbsup:
Marco O.: thanks — if p95 drops to within 20% of direct path we can consider making regional_prefer default for latency-sensitive models.
Tina Chen: initial canary started. initial 10min snapshot: H100(us-west canary): p50 90ms p95 250ms (down from 380) | A100(eu-west canary): p50 120ms p95 280ms (down from 520) — kernel_set metric shows fused_v3 pinned.
Jia Li: excellent — looks like kernel pin + prefer regional reduced tail. continuing to monitor.
Rachel S.: great signal. let's schedule a small follow-up retro to document ops knobs and update the onboarding checklist for new models (kernel_hint, routing_sensitivity).
Tina Chen: noted. will open a doc and a short runbook PR after we confirm 1h stable.
Marco O.: rolling this discussion into the model onboarding checklist will save us future cycles. thanks team.
